recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. The current FHIR source satisfies the published issue, and adding more prose would duplicate existing normative guidance without changing implementer understanding.
issue_request: FHIR-13836 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core search change request for STU3. It asked the search page to clarify that if _type is included in a root-level search, all other search parameters SHALL be common to all provided types, and if _type is not included, all parameters SHALL be common to all resource types.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites svn revision 13878. In the current git history this is commit 5d3347c67a57eeedfa55827c86442aa70a333a64, 'GF#13836 - note about cross search parameters', which added the requested wording to source/search.html. Later search-page refactors, including 83529ed121dc9fc1d9aeb117b0fe8a6293f9f0c9, moved and reformatted the rule into the current Search Contexts section without changing its meaning.
additional_context: The original Zulip thread linked from the Jira confirms the intended distinction: _type narrows the resource set, so other parameters must be common to those listed types; without _type, parameters must be common to all resources. Earlier FHIR-core issues FHIR-5700 and FHIR-10459 explain the root-search baseline and URL form, but do not conflict with this later _type clarification. No Confluence reference or later conflicting community evidence was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/search.html currently states the SHALL rule at lines 297-300 and the _type section gives an example where _type=Observation,Condition&patient=Patient/123 is valid because patient is valid on both resource types.
